# Datasets

## Libraries

```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("patchwork")
```

## Import of genetic cluster information

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
ivip_to_genetic_clusters <- read.csv(file = "../../../../00.info/02.genetic_structure_jonathan_dijon/faba_bean_ivip_and_genetic_cluster.csv", 
                          header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, sep =",") 

```

## Import of A. fabae phenotyping screen data

Two data files:\
- The first is the complete dataset *unfiltered*.\
- The second is the filtered dataset, where filters have been applied:\
\* If no surviving adult was found, then observation was removed.\
\* If one adult was present but without any larvae, then the observation was removed.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

fabae_raw <- read.csv(file = "../../../../01.data/2023_screen_specifics_251genotypes/02.aphis_fabae_on_faba_collection/aphis_fabae_fecundity_on_faba_collection_2024-04-02.csv", 
                   header = TRUE, 
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

fabae_filtered <- read.csv(file = "../../../01.GWAS/01_phenotipic_analysis/01.dataset_filtering/01_A.fabae/final filters/aphis_fabae_data_filtered_6.csv", 
                   header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, sep =",")

```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

fabae_raw_nrows <- nrow(fabae_raw)
fabae_raw_ngenotypes <- length(unique(fabae_raw$ivip))

fabae_filtered_nrows <- nrow(fabae_filtered)
fabae_filtered_ngenotypes <- length(unique(fabae_filtered$ivip))
```

::: callout-important
The complete data set contains `r fabae_raw_nrows` rows and `r fabae_raw_ngenotypes` genotypes.\
The filtered data set contains `r fabae_filtered_nrows` rows and `r fabae_filtered_ngenotypes` genotypes.
:::

# Comparison of proportions of genetic clusters in the raw and filtered dataset

## List of IVIPs in original panel and raw/filtered A. fabae dataset

```{r}
ivips_in_clusters <- unique(ivip_to_genetic_clusters$ivip)
ivips_in_raw_fabae_dataset <- unique(fabae_raw$ivip)
ivips_in_filtered_dataset <- unique(fabae_filtered$ivip)
```

## Data extraction

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

counts_per_genetic_cluster_total <- 
  ivip_to_genetic_clusters %>% 
  select(ivip, cluster_name) %>%
  group_by(cluster_name) %>%
  summarise(n_total = n()) 

```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

counts_per_genetic_cluster_raw <- 
  fabae_raw %>%
  inner_join(ivip_to_genetic_clusters, by = "ivip") %>%
  select(ivip, cluster_name) %>%
  distinct() %>% 
  group_by(cluster_name) %>%
  summarise(n_raw = n()) 
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

counts_per_genetic_cluster_filtered <-
  fabae_filtered %>%
  inner_join(., ivip_to_genetic_clusters, by = "ivip") %>%
  select(ivip, cluster_name) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(cluster_name) %>%
  summarise(n_filtered = n())

```

```{r}
combined_counts_per_cluster <- inner_join(counts_per_genetic_cluster_total, 
                                         counts_per_genetic_cluster_raw, 
                                         by = "cluster_name") %>%
  inner_join(counts_per_genetic_cluster_filtered, by = "cluster_name") %>% 
  # remove row if cluster_name == NAs
  filter(!is.na(cluster_name)) 
  

head(combined_counts_per_cluster, n = 10)
```

## Pie chart

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

plot_order = c("n_total", "n_raw", "n_filtered")

p_pie_charts <- combined_counts_per_cluster %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("n_"), 
               names_to = "dataset", 
               values_to = "n_total") %>%
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, levels = plot_order)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n_total, fill = cluster_name)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
  # add numbers
  geom_text(aes(label = n_total), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3) +
  coord_polar("y") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "right") + 
  facet_wrap(~ dataset, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1"); p_pie_charts

```

## Barplot

Often a barplot is much easier to compare.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

p_barplot <- combined_counts_per_cluster %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("n_"), 
               names_to = "dataset", 
               values_to = "n_total") %>%
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, levels = plot_order)) %>% 
  # Make a stacked barplot per cluster
  ggplot(aes(x = cluster_name, y = n_total, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  labs(x = "Genetic cluster", 
       y = "Number of genotypes") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  facet_wrap( ~ dataset, scales = "free_y") +
  # Add numbers at the tip of each  bar
  geom_text(aes(label = n_total), 
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), 
            size = 3, 
            color = "black"); p_barplot
```

Combined plot (pie chart + barplots)

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false

p_pie_charts + p_barplot + 
  plot_layout(ncol = 1) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Distribution of genotypes in genetic clusters (A. fabae)")

```

::: callout-important
We see that the proportions are not different between the complete set of genotypes (N=248), the set of genotypes from which observations of aphid fecundity were made and the final filtered dataset.
:::
